match.reason: The closest bank point, Nominalisation, covers turning verbs and adjectives into nouns, but the new point is about building long noun groups with modifiers to condense information, which is a related but different idea.

draft.title: Condensing information with noun groups
card: A noun group is a noun plus the words that describe it. It can be short, such as the dog, or long, such as the loud, scruffy dog from next door.
Writers add describing words before the noun and extra detail after it. One long noun group can hold facts that would otherwise need a whole sentence.
Nominalisation turns a verb or an adjective into a noun. Grow becomes growth, and decide becomes decision. This lets an action or quality be treated as a thing.

Compare: Online shopping has grown quickly. With a nominalised noun group it becomes the rapid growth of online shopping. The idea now fits inside one noun group, so it can be the subject of a sentence. Formal and academic writing uses this often.
draft.remember: Noun groups and nominalisation pack more information into fewer words.

a.q: Which choice shows nominalisation, turning a verb into a noun?
opts: The council decided becomes the council's decision
The council decided becomes the council quickly decided
The council decided becomes the council had decided
The council decided becomes the council did decide
a.why: Decided is a verb, and decision is the noun made from it. The other options only change the verb or add an adverb, so the action is not turned into a thing.
a.clue: Look for the option where the action becomes a noun.

b.q: Kiran rewrites: Cities have expanded fast, and this harms the bush around them. Which rewrite condenses the information best into one noun group as the subject?
opts: The fast expansion of cities harms the surrounding bush
Cities expand fast and so they harm the surrounding bush
Cities have expanded quickly and the bush is being harmed
The bush is harmed because the cities expanded so quickly
b.why: Expansion is made from the verb expand, and the whole idea sits in one noun group as the subject. In the other options the action is still a verb, so the information is not packed into one noun group.
b.clue: Find the option that starts with a noun group built from the verb expand.

a.best: The council decided becomes the council's decision

b.best: The fast expansion of cities harms the surrounding bush
